reading.body:
The graph underlying this site contains 25,832 documented edges, and the single largest contributor is the link between models and the papers their authors cite, accounting for 8,543 of those connections.

The model-to-paper edges outnumber every other relationship type combined by a wide margin. They are sourced from arXiv identifiers that model authors placed in their own Hub tags, which means the attribution is self-reported rather than inferred. The next largest edge type, model-to-modality-section, adds 16,369 entries, so together those two categories alone account for roughly 96 percent of all edges in the graph. The remaining nine relationship types, covering lawsuits, MCP servers, products, Form D filings, patents, SEC registrations, people, APIs, and vendor feeds, each sit below 340 edges.

That skew reflects what is actually measurable at scale. Model metadata and paper identifiers exist in structured, machine-readable registries. Legal and financial relationships require record-by-record verification, which the methods notes confirm: SEC registrants are verified within seven days, patent counts are described as floors rather than totals, and lawsuit defendants are matched against a docket tracker. The data does not speak to the magnitude of compute or capital behind any individual relationship, only to the existence of the relationship itself. A company appearing once in the Form D set and once in the lawsuit set may represent vastly different levels of activity; the edge count does not distinguish between them.
